items.question: Why is the Kula way reviled by those who do not recognize it?
premises: Beasts are those bound in ignorance.
Such beings lack recognition of Kula.
What is not recognized is reviled.
items.inference: The Kula duty is reviled by unknowing bound beings.
uncertainties: vigahītaḥ can mean censured or investigated; context favors reviled.
items.plain_english: The Kula way is reviled by ignorant bound beings who do not recognize it.

items.question: What does not arise for one who reviles the Kula way?
premises: Reviling Kula shows lack of recognition.
Guru compassion is needed for Kula knowledge.
Without that openness, Kula knowledge does not arise.
items.inference: For such a person, neither guru compassion nor Kula knowledge arises.
items.plain_english: For him, neither the guru's compassion nor knowledge of Kula arises.

items.question: Why do some people fail to know Kula despite its presence?
premises: Kula can be known.
Some people are deluded by divine power.
Delusion prevents recognition.
items.inference: Those deluded by the Goddess do not know Kula.
uncertainties: tava may refer to the Goddess addressed or to her Kula.
items.plain_english: Thus, deluded by me, they do not know your Kula.

items.question: What do deluded humans pursue instead of Kula?
premises: Deluded humans do not know Kula.
They still engage in pursuits.
Their pursuits yield fruitless effort.
items.inference: Deluded humans continually pursue things that bear only vain effort as fruit.
items.plain_english: And people always pursue things whose fruits are nothing but vain effort.

items.question: How do foolish people respond to the vision dear to the Goddess?
premises: The Kula vision is dear to the Goddess.
Fools lack recognition of it.
What fools do not recognize they revile.
items.inference: Fools revile the Goddess's beloved vision.
items.plain_english: Alas, alas, fools revile your vision, which is dear to me.

items.question: Why do those proud of knowledge fail to know the Kula duty?
premises: True knowledge of Kula requires recognition.
Some people are falsely proud of knowledge.
False pride obstructs recognition.
items.inference: Those vainly proud of knowledge do not know the Kula duty.
items.plain_english: Those who are vainly proud of their knowledge do not know the Kula way.

rows.grounds: having taken another body or form

items.question: For what purpose does one take another form in relation to the wicked?
premises: The wicked are opposed to Kula.
Divine power can assume other forms.
Such assumption can serve to delude the wicked.
items.inference: Another form is taken in order to delude the wicked.
uncertainties: The subject taking another form is implicit from context.
items.plain_english: Indeed, taking another form, it is for the delusion of the wicked.

rows.grounds: even over immense spans of time

items.question: What is the fate of the wicked who revile Kula over vast time?
premises: The wicked are deluded regarding Kula.
Spiritual progress requires recognition.
Even immense time does not remove this obstruction.
items.inference: For them there is no progress even in hundreds of crores of ages.
uncertainties: gatir may mean spiritual progress or final liberation.
items.plain_english: And for them there is no progress, even in hundreds of crores of ages.

items.question: How does a meritorious person respond to obstacles against Kula?
premises: Some people are restrained from Kula.
A meritorious person recognizes its value.
Recognition leads to steadfast resort.
items.inference: Even when restrained, a meritorious person resorts to Kula alone.
items.plain_english: Even when restrained, a meritorious person still resorts to Kula alone.

rows.grounds: sages, masters of yoga, and others

items.question: What have sages and yogic masters attained through Kula?
premises: Sages and yogic masters seek supreme accomplishment.
Kula leads to supreme accomplishment.
Such beings have attained it.
items.inference: Sages, yogic lords, and others have attained the highest success.
items.plain_english: Sages, lords of yogis, and others have attained the highest supreme accomplishment.

items.question: Who are considered great and extremely rare among practitioners?
premises: The Kaula way is difficult to follow.
Some truly serve the Kaula way.
Such dedication is rare and exalted.
items.inference: Those who serve the Kaula way are great and extremely rare.
items.plain_english: Those who truly serve the Kaula way are great and exceedingly rare.

rows.grounds: skilled in the reality of Kula

items.question: How rare is one who is expert in the truth of Kula?
premises: Knowledge of Kula truth is difficult.
Few attain expertise in it.
Such expertise is therefore rare.
items.inference: An expert in the truth of Kula is rare.
items.plain_english: O great Goddess, this expert in the truth of Kula is rare.
